tweets.text:
Massively underestimated:

The “cost” of people coming to work knowing things are broken & fearing the next thing breaking.

This holds for usability issues, “bugs”, “quality”, elephants in the room, strategy misalignment...anything.

The drag and dissonance is extremely costly.
design and developers weigh in on the "best" product manager they've worked with...

One of the big shifts. When the c-suite have seen — with their own eyes:

1) a usability test in person
2) a feature tested & pulled
3) teams connect directly w/users/customers
4) a team a team truly iterate
5) high quality
6) a real product strategy

Massive difference.

pmtip ...

97.5% of ideas/options/things don't need to be in a "ticketing system". The "ticketing system" is not a great place for interrelated ideas, concepts, research, maps, etc.

None of them are built for that.

Wrong tool for the job.

good exercise with team ... list out frequently used words that seem to cause confusion/misunderstanding. Recent exercise:

MVP
Vision
P0
Tested
Usable
Experiment
Strategy
Objective, Key Result
Extended Team
Agile
Accountability
Back of the napkin estimate
Lead
Dependency

Ppl tend to respond to “big problems” w/ “big plans”

When typically w/a big problem there are numerous oppportunities for quick wins and rapid improvement.

Issue? “Big plans” are the currency of many orgs. It is easier to get support for a big plan than continuous improvement.

23yo just told me that “investors are the real customers and the company is the product”.

I don’t think he was joking.

Quick fix for 2020

Relabel your “done” column and/or add a column for measuring/monitoring.

For each item, do a quick review. What have you learned?

Done is rarely done.
